name: South Carolina

jury_list.statute: S.C. Code 14-7-1530: 'The clerk of court shall maintain a list of all jurors who are excused or disqualified by the presiding judge and state the reasons given by the presiding judge for excusing or disqualifying the jurors.' 14-7-1010 has the same duty for each term. No section opens or closes that list. Status: null.

sources.cite: S.C. Code 14-7-130 (jury list built from DMV records of 'citizens of the United States' merged with registered voters)
S.C. Code 14-7-1530 (clerk keeps a list of excused or disqualified jurors with reasons)
S.C. Code 14-7-1010 (clerk keeps a list of jurors excused or disqualified, with reasons, signed by the presiding judge)
S.C. Code 14-7-810 (listed disqualifications; no citizenship item)
S.C. Att'y Gen. Op. to Robert L. McCurdy (Aug. 4, 2014) ('it is not at all clear that the court system is included within the reach of FOIA'; grand juror names likely exempt)

voter_file.who_may_get: Official registration records are public records open to inspection by any citizen (S.C. Code 7-5-410). The State Election Commission sells precinct lists to a qualified elector (7-3-20(D)(13)).

sources.cite: S.C. Code 7-3-20(D)(13) (precinct lists to a qualified elector at reasonable price)
S.C. Code 7-5-410 (official registration records are public records open to inspection by any citizen)

private_challenge.who: Any person; 7-5-230(A) does not limit who may challenge.
private_challenge.form_or_statute: S.C. Code 7-5-230(A): challenges to a registered elector's qualifications (other than at the polls) must be made in writing to the county board of voter registration and elections. The board gives notice to the elector and the challenger, holds a hearing within 10 days, accepts evidence, and rules under 7-5-120.
private_challenge.evidence_standard: The board accepts evidence at a hearing (7-5-230(A)). No standard stated.

county_board.name: South Carolina county voter registration and election offices
county_board.note: Written challenges under 7-5-230 go to the county board.

audit_path.statute: S.C. Code 30-4-30 (Freedom of Information Act) and 52 U.S.C. 20507(i) (NVRA public inspection of list-maintenance records)
audit_path.what_you_can_request: Counts only, from the State Election Commission or the county board of voter registration and elections: per year, the number of registrants matched to the DMV monthly report of non-U.S. citizens issued a license or ID (7-3-70(c)), and the number of those registrations cancelled; and the number of written challenges under 7-5-230 on citizenship grounds and their outcomes.
audit_path.note: Do not ask for names. No South Carolina statute sends the 14-7-1530 list to election officials. The Attorney General said in 2014 that FOIA's reach to the courts is 'not at all clear', so do not ask the clerk of court for jury records.

gates.basis: Jury records: the clerk keeps a list of excused or disqualified jurors with reasons (14-7-1530), but no statute says whether it is public (null), so counts only. A written challenge to the county board is allowed, with a hearing within 10 days (S.C. Code 7-5-230). Strict gates.

No voter_file value changes.

Flag (PA-style suspect): 14-7-1530 and 14-7-1010 require a written list of every juror excused or disqualified, with the judge's reasons. This is like Pennsylvania's list (42 Pa.C.S. 4523(a)), but no South Carolina section opens it for inspection. The Attorney General wrote on Aug. 4, 2014 that 'it is not at all clear that the court system is included within the reach of FOIA'. public stays null (treated as confidential). Reopen only on a statute or ruling that opens the list. See REQ-NOTE 46. Reopen candidate (Optimus 2026-10-07: null stays). See review/REOPEN.md.

Qualification wording: 14-7-810 lists disqualifications (felony, English, infirmity, education) but no citizenship item. Citizenship enters through the source list: 14-7-130 uses DMV records of persons who are 'citizens of the United States' merged with registered voters.

official_pipeline is null: no South Carolina statute sends juror citizenship information to election officials. The DMV sends the State Election Commission 'a monthly report of all non-United States citizens who are issued a driver's license or identification card' (7-3-70(c)). That is a DMV pipeline, kept in audit_path.
Cancelled-voter file: no published South Carolina cancelled-voter file with a jury reason code was found. REQ-NOTE 27 drops cancelled rows before matching.
dob_in_public_file and registration_date_in_public_file are null: the sections read do not list public fields.
